Offing, Slipway, and Seaworthy

Three tools share the work on a Slipway-shaped Jekyll site for GitHub Pages. Each one owns a different question. Use them in order so an agent (or a human) does not mix lifecycle evidence with site verification.

Tool Owns Maturity
Offing Whether a gem, npm package, GitHub Action, or runtime line is deprecated or end-of-life, with evidence Shipped (offing on npm)
Slipway The Jekyll theme, layout, and Pages-oriented site stack In planning and dogfooding; use only what its repository documents
Seaworthy Whether the built site is healthy (links, agent-readable structure) Pre-alpha; not on npm yet — commands below are for when its first release ships

Offing and Seaworthy both run locally against files on disk. Neither sends your repository to a cloud service during a check or verify.

The agent loop

Work in this order when you change dependencies or site content.

1. Before adding a gem, package, or Action

Check the dependency with Offing before you edit Gemfile, package.json, or workflow uses: pins.

npx @velella/offing check pkg:rubygems/jekyll@4.3.4
npx @velella/offing check pkg:npm/typescript@5.4.5
npx @velella/offing check pkg:github/actions/checkout@v4

Or, if the CLI is on your PATH as offing:

offing check pkg:rubygems/jekyll@4.3.4
  • If the result is affected, prefer the replacement Offing names and cite its evidence links. Do not add the dependency without telling the user why.
  • version-dependent means the answer depends on the version — call again with the version you intend to lock.
  • no-data means Offing has no rule for that package; it is not a claim that the package is safe.

For Ruby gems on a Pages site, also keep an eye on the Ruby runtime line (.ruby-version, Gemfile, Gemfile.lock) — GitHub Pages builds with a fixed Ruby line that must still receive fixes.

2. Edit pages and configuration

Change Markdown, _config.yml, layouts, and workflows as the task requires. Slipway-specific behavior follows the Slipway repository and starter; do not assume features that are not documented there.

Copy the Offing CI starter when the site has no lifecycle gate yet: examples/starters/slipway/.

3. After the site builds

When _site/ exists from bundle exec jekyll build (or your CI build step), verify the output with Seaworthy:

# Pending Seaworthy's first npm release — not installable yet.
seaworthy verify ./_site

Until Seaworthy publishes, treat this step as documentation-only. Do not fail a task because the command is unavailable.

Which output to trust for what

Question Trust Do not use
Is this gem, package, or Action deprecated or end-of-life? Offing check (or repository scan) — lifecycle rules with sources Seaworthy
Are links broken or pages hard for agents to read on the built site? Seaworthy verify (once released) Offing
What is already declared in this repo? Offing scan on the tree — findings at exact paths A single check for everything

Offing answers lifecycle questions with reviewed rules. Seaworthy answers site quality questions on static HTML. A clean Offing scan does not mean the site links work; a passing Seaworthy run does not mean a new gem is safe to add.

Wire this into your agent

Copy examples/agents/site-stack/AGENTS.md into the site repository (merge with your existing AGENTS.md if you already have one). It repeats the loop in imperative form for coding agents.
